_comment: Machine-readable model recommendations. Read by bin/llm-install and bin/llm-recommend. Edit this file, not the markdown — the docs quote it, so two copies would drift. Every row carries whether it was actually measured or merely extrapolated; saying 'verified' about an untested recommendation is how a tool stops being trustworthy.

budget._comment: Converts total RAM into a safe maximum on-disk model size. Best-effort heuristic, not a simulator — on a Compute error, step down a tier rather than trusting the arithmetic.
budget.worked_example: 36GB, IDE open, 8K ctx -> (36-4-4) - 5.4 - 0.5 = 22.1 ; /1.15 = 19.2 GB ceiling. Matches the measured fact that an 18GB model + 8K ctx still OOM'd here when other processes held wired memory.

tiers.note: Chat and autocomplete only. Too small to hold a tool schema plus working context reliably — agentic loops will thrash.
Short, single-file tasks. No MoE headroom at this tier.
qwen3-coder:30b fits on paper but leaves almost no headroom once a browser and IDE are open.

30B MoE, 3B active per token — 30B knowledge at 3B speed. Measured on an M4 Max/36GB: loads, serves, and emits correct structured tool calls. Close to the ceiling: a second model or a forgotten llama-cli session will OOM it.
Same pick as 36GB but with real headroom for longer context.
Room for a much larger context window, or a second model resident alongside.
Extrapolated. Check disk before pulling — 65GB is a serious download.
qwen3-coder:480b exists but at Q4 exceeds most SSDs. Not recommended without a deliberate disk plan.

embedding.note: Tiny. Pull alongside the primary if you want local RAG.

known_bad.note: ollama rejects it at the API: 'does not support tools' (HTTP 400). Through llama-server it is worse — it emits tool calls as template TEXT and then hallucinates the tool output, reporting success for files it never wrote. Chat only.
A -base tag is not instruction-tuned. It continues text rather than answering. Use the instruct/default tag.
arch 'dflash' is a DSpark DRAFT model, not standalone. llama.cpp needs ctx_other, which b12034 does not expose. Only usable as the draft half of speculative decoding.

quantisation.rule: Quantise deeper to fit a BIGGER model; never deeper on the same model. A 30B at Q4_K_M beats a 14B at Q8. Below Q4, code specifically falls apart — one mangled bracket breaks the whole output, where prose would degrade gracefully.
quantisation.prefer_moe: A 30B-A3B activates 3B params per token: large-model knowledge at small-model speed, for the storage cost of the full model. On a memory-constrained Mac this beats a dense model of the same size.

qwen3-coder:30b.with_system_message: FAIL — emits a tool call as text
qwen3-coder:30b.note: Only a system role breaks it: ollama's template injects the tool definitions into the system slot, so a user-supplied system message displaces them. An earlier reading blamed tool history as well; the probe shows that is wrong — tool history is fine. llm-agent folds the system prompt into the first user turn, which is the correct fix.
